impact.affected_asset: ERC-20 deposit liquidity and the corresponding Compact accounting credit.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a configured token callback to re-enter The Compact's deposit path and obtain credit derived from an overlapping balance-delta interval when the reported guard bypass conditions hold.
impact.security_effect: Over-crediting of deposited ERC-20 value, enabling double-spending of a deposit under the report's specific one-time activation circumstances.

causal_trace.summary: A callback-capable token can invoke configured calldata on The Compact from transferFrom before completing the token transfer.

The reported deposit routine snapshots the Compact's balance before safeTransferFrom and credits the post-transfer balance delta; nested deposits can share the same initial snapshot when the intended reentrancy exclusion is bypassed during TSTORE activation.

In the affected wrapper, a nonzero Tstorish guard value blocks entry and clearing delegates to _clearTstorish. The report identifies a one-time bypass associated with switching the Tstorish backing from persistent to transient storage after support becomes available.

The report's nested example credits 20 in the inner call and 40 in the outer call after 40 tokens are transferred, producing 60 newly credited value; it characterizes this as double-spending a deposit.

failure.operation: Nested balance-delta deposit accounting after callback reentry during the Tstorish guard-mode activation condition.

primary_invariant.statement: Each token balance increase used by a deposit flow must be credited once, and the balance-before/balance-after interval must not be concurrently reused by a nested deposit.
primary_invariant.violated_because: safeTransferFrom occurs between the initial-balance snapshot and balance-delta crediting, while the report identifies a lifecycle-specific bypass of the Tstorish-backed guard that permits a callback to re-enter this interval.

provenance.source_id: Spearbit Uniswap The Compact Security Review §5.3.1

quality.review_notes: The report supplies a concrete accounting trace and marks the remediation verified, while the inspected project helper supplies a callback mechanism. No supplied artifact establishes an executed finding-specific regression test or reproduction under the narrow chain-upgrade and activation prerequisites. The underlying pre-fix Tstorish activation implementation is not present, so the exact state transition is not reconstructed here.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fixed guard treats only values greater than 1 as locked and writes sentinel value 1 rather than clearing the guard slot, retaining state that distinguishes prior entry while permitting subsequent non-reentrant calls.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The report limits the bypass to a one-time activation circumstance after a pre-transient-storage deployment; a callback-capable token must invoke a nested Compact call during token collection.
data_structure_invariants: A reentrancy-guard sentinel must preserve exclusion across its backing-mode lifecycle.
A token-balance snapshot must correspond to exactly one credited transfer interval.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report's exploit scenario is conditional on the one-time Tstorish activation path; exact activation constraints are not available in the bundled Tstorish code.
numeric_domains.name: reentrancy guard sentinel

state_context.state_machine: The guard uses a Tstorish abstraction that the report says initially falls back to persistent storage when transient storage is unsupported and can later activate transient-storage use. The exact Tstorish activation code is not in the bundle.
